fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the road at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under poor visibility or at night can identify it without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain at least 14 feet of horizontal clearance and sufficient overhead clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Clear vegetation from both sides of the access drive so responders can see the route ahead and move without obstruction.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the residence or detached structure so fire and medical vehicles can exit without backing the full length of the drive.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Cut back dense vegetation that grows directly against or immediately alongside the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the buildings on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation between the residence and the detached structure to open a clear path between the two buildings for responders on foot.
• Keep the walkway clear of overgrowth so responders can move quickly between the front and sides of the property.
• If a gate controls the access drive, keep it unlocked or install a Knox padlock so responders can enter without delay.
• Post a property map or address placard near the driveway entrance showing the location of the residence,

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees closest to the structure to create open gaps between the tree canopy and the building.
• Break up the tree cluster near the structure by removing some trees to create separation between them and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls of the structure.
• Cut back brush in the area adjacent to the structure to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the building.
• Clear woody debris, including fallen branches, logs, and dead plant material, from around the structure and outbuildings.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep the full width and height of the driveway clear for vehicle access.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and vegetation growing along the edges of the driveway that are narrowing the travel path.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches and debris that could block emergency vehicle movement.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the structure to create open space and allow movement around the building.
• Thin vegetation along the limited rear access area to allow a person to move around the back of the structure without obstruction.
• Remove dead material from within shrub groupings scattered around the property.
